privacy_1: This site sets no cookie, and keeps nothing in your browser but the language you choose in its header. It loads nothing from another site: its fonts, images and scripts are served with it.
privacy_2: It counts its visits with Umami Cloud, in the European Union (Frankfurt), without cookie. For each page seen: the page, the page you came from, your browser, system and kind of device, your screen's size, your language and your country. Your IP address is used to tell your country and to tell visits apart, and is not kept with them. The counts are kept six months, used only to know what is read, and never sold or shared. Umami's policy: umami.is/privacy.

title_home: Lantern · An open protocol for game library servers
description_home: Lantern is an open, versioned protocol between the game library servers people run at home for their own games and the homebrews and apps that read them, on every platform Aurore runs on. Draft {draft}.
description_spec: The Lantern protocol, draft {draft}: platforms and their profiles, discovery, pairing, the library, downloads checked by SHA-256, game data, homebrew and game ports, save backups and their encryption, cheats, events, sharing on the LAN, sync, static libraries, errors and limits.
footer_license: The specification's text under CC BY 4.0, everything else under MIT.
hero_title: From your server to your console, one open protocol.
hero_lede: Lantern is an open, versioned contract between the library servers people run at home for their own games and the homebrews and apps that read them, on a console, a phone, a computer or in the browser: browse the library, download with integrity checks, install homebrew, keep save backups and cheats.
status_text: The text may still change before 1.0. Comments are welcome, from client and server authors especially.
solid_title: What it covers, and what makes it solid
solid_lede: Lantern starts fresh: it is compatible with no earlier protocol, so every choice serves safety and the long run. Draft {draft} is the current text, and each earlier draft stays readable as it was published.
solid_versions: Versioned twice, in the path and in every document: a change never breaks a client in silence.
solid_tokens: A token per device, approved on the server and revocable one by one: no password is ever typed on the console or kept there.
solid_https: HTTPS everywhere. A server at home with its own certificate is pinned when the console pairs, once you have compared its key's fingerprint on both screens.
solid_features: Declared features: the server says what it offers, to whom, and in which schema.
solid_suite: A conformance suite that checks a server from outside, and a reference server that passes it.
solid_errors: Errors with real status codes, all in one format.
solid_nothing: Nothing hidden: no hardware identifier, no proprietary encryption, no change to the client decided by the server.
implement_lede: The specification is short: few routes, fixed shapes, plain HTTP and JSON.
server_text: Serve the handshake and the library, and pairing when your server is private; add game data, homebrew, save backups, cheats or events when you want, and declare them in its features. A server fits in a weekend, and a library you only read can be plain files.
client_text: Find servers on the local network, name your platform, read their features, page through the library and check each download's SHA-256. A client fits in a few hundred lines of C++.
first_client: The first client will be PlayShelf, a homebrew package manager for the Nintendo Switch.
own_text: Lantern carries what your server holds, between it and your console. It finds nothing and distributes nothing: it is not a way to get games, and its servers are for the games you own.
licence_text: The specification's text: share and adapt it, naming where it comes from.
licence_rest: Everything else (schemas, OpenAPI description, examples, conformance suite, reference server), so that any server or client, under any licence, can implement the protocol and copy its schemas as they are.
licence_compatible: Questions, comments and proposals go to the repository's issues.
privacy_more: Who publishes this site, who hosts it, and how to ask about your data:
closing_text: The draft is the time to change things. An issue about a route, a field or a missing case helps every server and client to come.
spec_lede: REST and JSON, versioned by path and by a schema in every document. Twenty-one short sections, and annexes for the platforms, for client authors and for the road to 1.0.
spec_english: The specification is written in English only, and the English text is the reference.
covers_quality: An id for every requirement, a threat model, conformance levels and the “Lantern compatible” badge, test vectors for libraries, and guidelines for clients.
covers_more: Errors and the server's message in your language, compressed JSON, Atlas ids, installed sizes, and withdrawing your own request.
conformance_title: Levels, a badge, and who passes
conformance_text: The suite prints the levels a server reaches, from Lantern Core to +deltas, and Lantern Static for a library of plain files. Every requirement of the text has an id, and the traceability page says which check of the suite covers it, and which ones only a client can keep.
description_demo: A public Lantern static library of fictional games, homebrew and cheat sets to point a client at, and its trapped variant, for testing clients.
demo_title: A library to point your client at
demo_lede: Games, homebrew and cheat sets that do not exist, served with this site as a Lantern static library: try a client without a server of your own.
demo_what: Everything in it is invented: its games, studios and people, with sheets and artwork drawn for them.
demo_files: Its files are placeholders of text, and its homebrew archives hold a README and nothing else: none of it is software, and nothing in it can be installed or run. One of them, Moss & Ember's, is half a megabyte, enough for a chunk index (§ 22 of the specification): try differential updates on it.
demo_point: Give your client this address. It asks the site for /.well-known/lantern first, finds none, then reads lantern.json: a handshake with static (§ 21 of the specification), pages of four items so that a client meets several, and every file by its SHA-256.
demo_suite: The conformance suite checks it at every build of this site, and it reaches Lantern Static:
demo_cors: GitHub Pages, which serves this site, answers every file with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *: a page on another site may read it with fetch(). Ask without credentials and without headers of your own (no Lantern-Platform: a static library's platform is in its paths), or the browser first sends a preflight request, which GitHub Pages does not answer.
demo_tracking: Its handshake and files carry no tracking: only this site's pages count their visits.
demo_trapped: Beside it, static libraries broken on purpose, one fault each, for testing clients: a file that is not its SHA-256, manifests that climb out of their folder or leave the platform's roots, a newer schema, documents too big or too deep, signatures that do not verify, a key of small order. Each one says what a client must do, and the conformance suite refuses them all.

flow_title: How Lantern carries a library: from your server at home, as versioned JSON with each file's SHA-256, to the consoles, phones, computers and browsers that read it.
flow_server_note: At home, with your own games
what_title: Your library, on every screen you play on
what_lede: One contract between the server you run and every homebrew or app that reads it, whoever wrote either of them.
how_title: Four steps, in plain HTTP and JSON
how_1_title: The server says what it offers.
how_1: Its handshake, at /.well-known/lantern, gives its versions, its platforms and the features it serves.
how_2: On a private server, you approve it there: it gets a token bound to the device, and no password is ever typed on the console.
how_3_title: It reads the library, page by page.
how_3: Every document carries its schema, and cursor pages neither skip nor repeat while the library changes.
how_4: The client checks each file's SHA-256 before installing anything, and a homebrew's signature when it has one.
how_more: Every route, field and error is in the text:
box_spec_text: Short sections and their annexes, every requirement with an id. In English, with an informative French translation.
box_schemas_text: A schema for every document, served at its own address, an example of each, and an OpenAPI description of the routes.
box_suite_text: Checks a server from outside and prints the levels it reaches, from Lantern Core to Lantern Static.
box_vectors_text: The bytes libraries must agree on: request signatures, fingerprints, paths, canonical JSON, encrypted backups, chunks.
box_server_text: A small server, on Python's standard library alone, that passes the suite and exports a static library.
box_sdk_text: Client and server libraries, in lantern-sdk: start from them rather than from scratch.
implement_registry: A server or client that passes the suite joins the registry, with the levels it reaches:
what_platforms_text: Nintendo Switch, New 3DS, PS Vita, PS4, Android, iOS and tvOS, Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser. A core that knows no platform, and a profile for each.
what_titles_text: Genres, players, age ratings, a summary and images in your language, read a hundred at a time.
what_homebrew_text: A manifest gives each file its place, nothing is written elsewhere without your consent, and an author's signature is checked when there is one. A port runs on the data of your own copy of the game, which Lantern never serves.
what_saves_text: Sent in chunks that survive a lost connection, and checked when they arrive.
what_cheats_text: Several sets for each version of a game, in each platform's own format.
what_static_text: A library as plain files, on GitHub Pages, a NAS or a USB key, which the reference server exports and the suite checks.
hero_changes: What changed since the last draft
feat_events: What changes on the server arrives as it happens, for a homebrew in the background or a home hub.
feat_deltas: An update reads only the chunks that changed, from the server, a mirror or a peer, each one checked.
feat_formats: A package says what it needs and what it contains: the server leaves out what the device cannot install.
feat_releases: Each version of the text is a release with its SHA-256 sums and build provenance, checked in one command.
feat_sharing: A console that holds a game passes it to another, with a grant from the server and every byte checked.
feat_sync: Wishes and installed games, merged item by item, only once you agree.
feat_e2e: Encrypted by the console, with a key the server never sees.
feat_keys: A key made at pairing signs every request: a copied token works nowhere else.
feat_admin: Invite a few devices for a few days, approve a console from your phone, cap the ratings.
proof_lede: Every Lantern server answers the same first request. The host below is a placeholder: use your own.
proof_note: An excerpt of the handshake (§ 4.2 of the specification), where each field is explained.

description_start: Read a Lantern library with curl in a minute, then pair a device and sign its requests: the path from the first request to the first download.
start_lede: Three commands against the demo library, three against a server of your own, and the whole path in one figure.
start_try_lede: The demo is a static library served with this site: nothing to install, nothing to sign in to.
start_1_text: Every library says what it is, which features it offers and its limits in one document.
start_2_text: A page of apps for one platform: each carries its size, its sha256 and the path of its file.
start_3_text: The file's SHA-256 is the one the app announced. A client refuses what does not match.
start_try_note: More to try, including libraries made to break a client:
start_server_title: Talk to a server of your own
start_server_lede: A server with accounts asks a device to pair first. These calls use a made-up address.
start_4_text: On a local network a client discovers it with a UDP datagram; with an address, it reads the handshake at a well-known path.
start_5_text: The server answers with a code to enter, on another device, where its owner signs in and approves.
start_6_text: With the token it gave, as a bearer; a device that paired with a key also signs each request.
start_path_lede: Step through it: each press lights one step and dims the rest.

spec_ask_title: Opens an issue on GitHub that names this section
description_check: Paste a handshake or any other document of a Lantern server and check it, in your browser, against the schemas this site publishes.
check_lede: Paste what a server answered and see whether it matches the schema it should: the same schemas the specification, the examples and the conformance suite use.
check_note: Nothing leaves your browser: the document is checked here, against the schemas this site serves.
check_newer: Its schema is newer than the one this site knows: a reader treats it as absent (§ 3.2) and never writes over it.
check_noscript: This page needs JavaScript to check a document in your browser. Without it, the schemas are at schemas/v1/ and tools/check_schemas.py checks a folder of examples.
description_examples: A signed request byte by byte, a pairing from its code to its token, and a grant: real exchanges built from the test vectors and the examples the suite checks.
examples_lede: What goes over the wire, with real bytes: nothing here is written by hand, it is read from the test vectors and examples that the repository checks.
examples_note: The keys, tokens and names are fictional test values (the key is RFC 8032's published test key), never real ones.
ex_sign_title: A signed request, byte by byte
ex_sign_text: A device paired with a key signs every request that carries its token. The server rebuilds the signature base from the request, and checks the signature with the key it bound to the token.
ex_sign_h_base: The signature base the device signs
ex_sign_h_refused: The same request without its signature
ex_pair_title: A pairing, from its code to its token
ex_pair_text: The device asks for a code and shows it; its owner approves on another device, signed in to the server; the device polls until the token is given, once.
ex_pair_h2: 2. The server answers with a code
ex_pair_h3: 3. The owner approves; the device polls
ex_grant_text: The server signs a short statement that a client may read one file; a peer that holds the file checks it with the server's public key, without asking anyone.
ex_grant_h_payload: What the server signs (JSON, keys in this order, no space)
ex_grant_h_grant: The grant: the payload and its signature, each in base64url
